card.name: Raqs Sharqi
card.tagline: Egypt's classical cabaret form of belly dance
card.profile: Raqs sharqi ('Eastern' or 'oriental dance') is the classical Egyptian style of belly dance that developed in Cairo during the first half of the 20th century, notably at Badia Masabni's Opera Casino (opened 1925). Per Wikipedia, it was shaped by film-era stars such as Taheyya Kariokka, Samia Gamal and Naima Akef, blending baladi and ghawazee folk movement with ballet-influenced use of the stage, travelling steps and lifted arms. It is the performance counterpart to the social raqs baladi.
card.insight: Raqs sharqi is regarded as the classical, codified form of Egyptian belly dance and the template for cabaret 'belly dance' worldwide (Wikipedia; World Dance Heritage).
